question: What is the effect of the provisions of sub-section (5) if a notice is personally served by the appellant on the Commissioner (Appeals)?
answer: The relief sought by the appellant in the appeal shall not be treated as having been given.

question: Can any period during which the hearing of an appeal is adjourned at the request of the appellant be excluded in the computation of the period of four months?
answer: Yes, the period shall be excluded in the computation of the period of four months.

question: What is the purpose of excluding any period during which the hearing of an appeal is adjourned on the request of the appellant?
answer: For the purposes of sub-section (5), any period during which the hearing of an appeal is adjourned on the request of the appellant shall be excluded in the computation of the period of four months referred to in that sub-section.

question: Who may be appointed as a judicial member of the Appellate Tribunal?
answer: A person may be appointed as a judicial member of the Appellate Tribunal if the person has exercised the powers of a District Judge and is qualified to be a Judge of the High Court; or is or has been an advocate of a High Court and is qualified to be a Judge of the High Court.

question: How many years of experience as Commissioner or Collector is required for a Commissioner Inland Revenue or Commissioner Inland Revenue (Appeals) to be eligible as an accountant member of an appellate tribunal?
answer: at least 3 years

question: What is the minimum period of professional practice required to be eligible as a chartered accountant for appointment as an accountant member of an appellate tribunal?
answer: not less than 10 years

question: What is the name of the Act that provides the definition of a cost and management accountant?
answer: Cost and Management Accountants Act,1966

question: How many members of the Appellate Tribunal should be in a Bench?
answer: not less than 2 members

question: Should a Bench of the Appellate Tribunal contain an equal number of judicial and accountant members?
answer: or so that the number of members of one class does not exceed the number of members of the other class by more than one.

question: Who can constitute a Bench consisting of a single member?
answer: The Chairperson may constitute as many benches consisting of a single member as he may deem necessary to hear such cases or class of cases as the Federal Government may by

question: What is the name of the Ordinance that established the Appellate Inland Revenue tribunal?
answer: Income Tax Ordinance 2001

question: When was Section 130 substituted through Tax Laws (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 2019?
answer: dated 26th December, 2019

question: What is the minimum number of members required to constitute a Bench in the Appellate Tribunal?
answer: Two members

question: What is the composition of a Bench in the Appellate Tribunal?
answer: A Bench must contain an equal number of judicial and accountant members, or so that the number of members of one class does not exceed the number of members of the other class by more than one.

question: Can the Federal Government direct how the powers of the Appellate Tribunal are exercised?
answer: Yes, the Federal Government may direct that all or any of the powers of the Appellate Tribunal shall be exercised by any one member, or more members than one, jointly or severally.

question: What is the maximum amount of tax or penalty for which a single member of the Appellate Tribunal may dispose of a case?
answer: One million rupees

question: How is a point decided when the members of a Bench differ in opinion?
answer: The point shall be decided according to the opinion of the majority of the members of the Bench.

question: What happens when the members of a Bench are equally divided on a point?
answer: The case shall be referred by the Chairperson for hearing on that point by one or more other members of the Appellate Tribunal.

question: Can the Chairperson constitute benches consisting of a single member?
answer: Yes, the Chairperson may constitute as many benches consisting of a single member as he may deem necessary to hear such cases or class of cases as the Federal Government may by order in writing, specify.

question: What happens to a case when the amount of tax or penalty involved does not exceed one million rupees?
answer: A single member of the Appellate Tribunal, authorized by the Chairperson, may dispose of the case.

question: What is the purpose of referring a case to other members of the Appellate Tribunal when the members of a Bench are equally divided on a point?
answer: To decide the point according to the opinion of the majority of the members of the Tribunal who have heard the case including those who first heard it.

question: What is the majority required to decide a point when the case is referred to other members of the Appellate Tribunal?
answer: The majority of the members of the Tribunal who have heard the case including those who first heard it.

question: What is the name of the Appellate Tribunal as per Section 130?
answer: The Appellate Tribunal Inland Revenue.

question: Who appoints the members of the Appellate Tribunal?
answer: The Federal Government.

question: What are the qualifications for a judicial member of the Appellate Tribunal Inland Revenue?
answer: The person must have been a Judge of a High Court, or been a District Judge, or be an advocate of a High Court with a standing of not less than ten years, or possess such other qualification as may be prescribed under sub-section (2) of this section.

question: Can the Federal Government appoint an additional member in the event of a tie?
answer: Yes, if there are an equal number of members of the Appellate Tribunal, the Federal Government may appoint an additional member for the purpose of deciding the case on which there is a difference of opinion.

question: What is the minimum experience required for a Commissioner Inland Revenue or Commissioner Inland Revenue (Appeals) to be eligible as an accountant member?
answer: Not less than three years.

question: How many years of professional practice as a chartered accountant is required for an accountant member?
answer: Not less than ten years.

question: What Ordinance regulates the procedure and functioning of the Appellate Tribunal?
answer: The Tax Laws (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 2019.

question: What should a person have to be eligible to be appointed as a member of the Appellate Tribunal?
answer: The person should be an advocate of a High Court for not less than fifteen years and possess such other qualification as may be prescribed.

question: Can rules regulating the Appellate Tribunal be made prior to the commencement of the Tax Laws (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 2019?
answer: Yes, the rules made prior to the commencement of the Tax Laws (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 2019 shall continue in force unless amended or repealed.

question: Who may prescribe rules for the Appellate Tribunal?
answer: The Prime Minister.

question: What is the minimum experience required to be eligible for appointment as a member of the Appellate Tribunal if one is an advocate of a High Court?
answer: fifteen years

question: Who can be appointed as the Chairman of the Appellate Tribunal?
answer: The Federal Government shall appoint any member possessing qualifications provided in clauses (a), (b), and (c) of sub-section (3) as Chairman of the Appellate Tribunal.

question: What is the minimum age at which a member of the Appellate Tribunal including the Chairman shall cease to hold office?
answer: sixty-two years

question: Can a member of the Appellate Tribunal including the Chairman resign?
answer: Yes, a member including the Chairman may resign or may be removed by the Federal Government, on the recommendation of performance review committee, to be constituted by the rules made under sub-section (2).

question: How long shall the Chairman of the Appellate Tribunal hold office?
answer: The Chairman shall hold office for a period of three years provided that the Federal Government may reappoint the Chairman for such further term or terms as it may deem appropriate.

question: What is the minimum experience required to be eligible for appointment as a member of the Appellate Tribunal if one is a chartered accountant?
answer: ten years

question: What is the procedure of the Appellate Tribunal Inland Revenue including constitution of benches, case management system, distribution of cases and other matters ancillary or incidental thereto regulated by?
answer: The rules made under sub-section (2).

question: Can the Federal Government reappoint the Chairman of the Appellate Tribunal?
answer: Yes, the Federal Government may reappoint the Chairman for such further term or terms as it may deem appropriate.

question: What are the grounds on which a member of the Appellate Tribunal including the Chairman may be removed by the Federal Government?
answer: in grounds, interalia, of inefficiency or misconduct, as prescribed by the rules made under sub-section (2).

question: How long shall the members falling under clauses (c) and (d) of sub-section (3) cease to hold office?
answer: on attaining the age of superannuation, under the law regulating their service

question: What is the Appellate Tribunal Inland Revenue responsible for?
answer: The procedure of the Appellate Tribunal Inland Revenue, including the constitution of benches, case management system, distribution of cases, and other matters ancillary or incidental thereto.

question: What is the basis for superannuation, as per Section 130 of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001?
answer: The age of superannuation, as the case may be, on grounds, inter alia, of inefficiency or misconduct, as prescribed by the rules made under sub-section (2).

question: What rules regulate the procedure of the Appellate Tribunal Inland Revenue?
answer: The rules made under sub-section (2).

question: What happens on grounds of inefficiency or misconduct?
answer: Superannuation may occur, as prescribed by the rules made under sub-section (2).

question: What are some examples of how the Appellate Tribunal Inland Revenue is organized?
answer: The constitution of benches and case management system are included.

question: What are the Appellate Tribunal Inland Revenue's primary responsibilities?
answer: Regulated by the rules made under sub-section (2), the primary responsibilities include case management and distribution of cases.

question: What powers does the Appellate Tribunal Inland Revenue have?
answer: None explicitly stated, but it is responsible for the procedure, including benches, case management, and distribution of cases.

question: How are superannuation grounds determined?
answer: On grounds of inefficiency or misconduct, as prescribed by the rules made under sub-section (2).

question: What is ancillary or incidental to the Appellate Tribunal Inland Revenue?
answer: Matters related to its procedure, including benches, case management, and distribution of cases.

question: What is the purpose of sub-section (2) in Section 130 of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001?
answer: To prescribe rules related to superannuation and the Appellate Tribunal Inland Revenue's procedure.

question: Who can appeal to the Appellate Tribunal?
answer: The taxpayer or the Commissioner can appeal to the Appellate Tribunal.

question: What is the prescribed fee for an appeal by a company?
answer: The prescribed fee for an appeal by a company is five thousand rupees.

question: Can an appeal be filed after the specified period?
answer: Yes, the Appellate Tribunal may admit an appeal after the expiration of the period if it is satisfied that the person appealing was prevented by sufficient cause from filing the appeal within that period.

question: How long does a taxpayer have to file an appeal?
answer: A taxpayer has sixty days to file an appeal to the Appellate Tribunal within the date of service of order of the Commissioner (Appeals).

question: Can tax be recovered while an appeal is pending?
answer: Yes, tax shall be payable in accordance with the assessment made in the case, unless recovery thereof has been stayed by the Appellate Tribunal.

question: What is the maximum period for which tax recovery can be stayed?
answer: The Appellate Tribunal may stay the recovery of tax for a period not exceeding one hundred and eighty days in aggregate.

question: How long does a person, other than an SOE, have to prefer an appeal to the Appellate Tribunal?
answer: Any person, other than an SOE, may prefer an appeal to the Appellate Tribunal within thirty days of the receipt of such order.

question: What is the prescribed fee for an appeal by a company under the substituted sub-section (1)?
answer: The prescribed fee for an appeal by a company is twenty thousand rupees.

question: Can a taxpayer directly appeal against the order of the Officer Inland Revenue or the Commissioner to the Appellate Tribunal?
answer: Yes, a taxpayer may directly appeal against the order of the Officer Inland Revenue or the Commissioner as the case may be to the Appellate Tribunal by exercising the option as provided in sub-section (1) of section 127.

question: Who is exempt from paying the prescribed fee except in the case of an appeal preferred by the Commissioner?
answer: No one is specifically mentioned as being exempt from paying the prescribed fee except in the case of an appeal preferred by the Commissioner.

question: What is the timeframe for appealing an order to the Appellate Tribunal?
answer: Within thirty days of the receipt of such order.

question: How can a taxpayer directly appeal an order to the Appellate Tribunal?
answer: By exercising the option as provided in sub-section (1) of section 127.

question: What is the prescribed fee for filing an appeal to the Appellate Tribunal?
answer: Twenty thousand rupees in case of a company and five thousand rupees in case other than a company.

question: Can an appeal be admitted after the expiration of the specified period?
answer: Yes, if the Appellate Tribunal is satisfied that the person preferring appeal was prevented by sufficient cause from filing the appeal within that period.

question: Does filing an appeal stay the recovery of tax?
answer: No, tax shall be payable in accordance with the assessment made in the case, unless recovery thereof has been stayed by the Appellate Tribunal.

question: How long can the Appellate Tribunal stay the recovery of tax?
answer: For ninety days, but the stay order shall cease to have effect if the taxpayer does not adhere to the hearing schedule for the appeal.

question: What happens if the Appellate Tribunal does not decide the appeal within the statutory period?
answer: The stay order under the second proviso shall not cease to have effect till finalization of the appeal by the Appellate Tribunal.

question: Can a Single Owner Entity (SOE) prefer an appeal under this sub-section?
answer: Yes, if sub-section (11) of section 134A applies.

question: What is the timeframe for preferring an appeal to the Appellate Tribunal after service of the order on the taxpayer?
answer: Within thirty days of the date of service of order on the taxpayer.

question: What are the conditions for filing an appeal to the Appellate Tribunal?
answer: The appeal shall be in the prescribed form, verified in the prescribed manner, accompanied by the prescribed fee, and preferred to the Appellate Tribunal within the specified period.

question: How many days does the Appellate Tribunal have to decide an appeal, as per Section 132?
answer: The Appellate Tribunal shall decide the appeal within ninety days of its filing.

question: What happens if an appeal is not decided within the specified period?
answer: The Appellate Tribunal shall seek condonation from the Minister of Law and Justice and such condonation shall not extend beyond ninety days.

question: What is the notice of alternative dispute resolution under Section 132?
answer: At the first hearing of appeal, the Appellate Tribunal shall bring to the notice of the taxpayer, the provisions relating to alternative dispute resolution under section 134A.

question: Can the Appellate Tribunal increase the amount of any assessment or penalty?
answer: No, the Appellate Tribunal shall not increase the amount of any assessment or penalty unless the taxpayer has been given a reasonable opportunity of showing cause against such increase.

question: What is the time limit for deciding an appeal, as per the substituted Section 132?
answer: The Appellate Tribunal shall decide the appeal within six months of its filing.

question: If a taxpayer declines the option of alternative dispute resolution, what happens next?
answer: The Appellate Tribunal shall fix date or dates for hearing and decision of the appeal in consultation with the taxpayer and Commissioner and in accordance with the rules.

question: Can the Appellate Tribunal remand a case to the Commissioner for making further enquiry or taking action?
answer: Yes, the Appellate Tribunal may remand the case to the Commissioner or the Commissioner (Appeals) for making such enquiry or taking such action as the Tribunal may direct.

question: How does the Appellate Tribunal communicate its order?
answer: The Appellate Tribunal shall communicate its order to the taxpayer and the Commissioner.

question: What is the cost that a taxpayer must pay for adjournment, as per Section 132?
answer: The Appellate Tribunal may deem fit to charge a cost of at least fifty thousand rupees for adjournment.

question: Is the decision of the Appellate Tribunal on an appeal final?
answer: Yes, save as provided in section 133, the decision of the Appellate Tribunal on an appeal shall be final.

question: What happens after the Appellate Tribunal renders a decision on an appeal?
answer: The decision of the Appellate Tribunal on an appeal shall be final, save as provided in section 133.

question: What is the Appellate Tribunal required to do regarding the hearing schedule?
answer: The Appellate Tribunal shall ensure strict adherence by the taxpayer and the Commissioner, to the hearing schedule as prescribed.

question: Can an adjournment be granted before the Appellate Tribunal?
answer: No, no adjournment shall be granted, except where there are compelling reasons for adjournment, to be recorded by the Appellate Tribunal, or on mandatory payment of such cost as the Appellate Tribunal may deem fit, which shall not be less than fifty thousand rupees.

question: What can the Appellate Tribunal do with an assessment order?
answer: The Appellate Tribunal may affirm, modify or annul the assessment order, remand the case to the Commissioner for making such enquiry or taking such action as the Tribunal may direct, or make such order as the Appellate Tribunal may deem fit.

question: When can the Appellate Tribunal increase or decrease an assessment or penalty?
answer: The Appellate Tribunal shall not increase the amount of any assessment or penalty or decrease the amount of any refund unless the taxpayer has been given a reasonable opportunity of showing cause against such increase or decrease, as the case may be.

question: Can the Appellate Tribunal make changes to an association's assessment?
answer: Yes, where, as the result of an appeal, any change is made in the assessment of an association of persons or a new assessment of an association of persons is ordered to be made, the Appellate Tribunal may authorize the Commissioner to amend accordingly any assessment order made on a member of the association.

question: What is the outcome when an appeal relates to a decision other than an assessment?
answer: The Appellate Tribunal may make an order to affirm, vary or annul the decision, and issue such consequential directions as the case may require.

question: Who receives the order of the Appellate Tribunal?
answer: The Appellate Tribunal shall communicate its order to the taxpayer and the Commissioner.

question: How much cost must be paid for an adjournment?
answer: The cost to be paid for an adjournment shall not be less than fifty thousand rupees.

question: Can the Appellate Tribunal make an order to remand a case to the Commissioner?
answer: Yes, the Appellate Tribunal may remand the case to the Commissioner for making such enquiry or taking such action as the Tribunal may direct.

question: What section of the Limitation Act, 1908 relates to an application under sub-section (1) of Section 133?
answer: Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1908 (IX of 1908) shall apply to an application under sub-section (1).

question: What is the minimum percentage of share capital required for a holding company to claim group relief in the case of a listed company?
answer: Fifty-five per cent

question: Can a company within the group engaged in the business of trading avail group relief?
answer: No

question: What is the time period within which a private limited company holding company with 75% ownership of share capital must get itself listed to claim group relief?
answer: Three years from the year in which loss is claimed

question: Are companies in the group required to comply with any specific corporate governance requirements to avail group relief?
answer: Yes, such corporate governance requirements and group designation rules or regulations as may be specified by the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan

question: Can a subsidiary company surrender its assessed losses for set off against income of the holding company for more than three tax years?
answer: No

question: What happens to unadjusted losses of a subsidiary company that are not adjusted against income of the holding company in the three tax years?
answer: The subsidiary company shall carry forward the unadjusted losses in accordance with section 57

question: Is the transfer of cash from the loss claiming company to the loss surrendering company a taxable event?
answer: No

question: Under what condition is the transfer of shares between companies and shareholders not considered a taxable event?
answer: If the transfer is to acquire share capital for formation of the group and approval of the Security and Exchange Commission of Pakistan or State Bank of Pakistan has been obtained

question: What is the consequence if the holding company disposes of shares during the five-year period, reducing its ownership to less than the required percentage?
answer: The holding company shall, in the year of disposal, offer the amount of profit on which taxes have not been paid due to set off of losses surrendered by the subsidiary company

question: Who must approve the transfer of cash from the loss claiming company to the loss surrendering company?
answer: The Board of Directors

question: What is the process when the Appellate Tribunal receives a High Court judgment?
answer: The Appellate Tribunal shall pass such orders as are necessary to dispose of the case conformably to the judgment.

question: What happens to the costs of a reference to the High Court under this section?
answer: The costs are at the discretion of the Court.

question: Can the tax due under an assessment be deferred if the High Court stays recovery?
answer: No, the tax due under the assessment shall be payable in accordance with the assessment unless recovery has been stayed by the High Court.

question: What is the fee required for an application under sub-section (1) by a person other than the Commissioner?
answer: One hundred rupees.

question: Which Act applies to an application under sub-section (1)?
answer: The Limitation Act, 1908 (IX of 1908)

question: What happens if an assessment is being appealed to the High Court and recovery of tax has not been stayed?
answer: The tax due under the assessment shall be payable in accordance with the assessment.

question: Is the Appellate Tribunal bound by a High Court judgment?
answer: Yes, the Appellate Tribunal must dispose of the case conformably to the judgment.

question: What is the requirement for a person other than the Commissioner to submit an application under sub-section (1)?
answer: A fee of one hundred rupees is required.

question: Can an application to the Appellate Tribunal be made after the relevant limitation period has expired?
answer: The Limitation Act, 1908 (IX of 1908) will apply to determine whether the application can be made.

question: How does the High Court's ruling affect the Appellate Tribunal's actions?
answer: The Appellate Tribunal must pass orders conformably to the High Court's judgment.

question: How long does an aggrieved person or the Commissioner have to file a reference to the High Court?
answer: Within ninety days of the communication of the order of the Appellate Tribunal.

question: What is required to be filed along with the reference to the High Court?
answer: The reference must be filed in the prescribed form along with a statement of the case.

question: What must the statement to the High Court set out?
answer: The statement to the High Court shall set out the facts, the determination of the Appellate Tribunal, and the question of law which arises out of its order.

question: How many judges of the High Court must hear a reference under this section?
answer: A Bench of not less than two judges of the High Court.

question: What happens to the Tribunal's order after the High Court decides a reference under this section?
answer: The Tribunal's order shall stand modified accordingly.

question: Can a reference be made to the High Court even if the tax is payable in accordance with the order of the Appellate Tribunal?
answer: Yes, a reference can be made to the High Court even if the tax is payable in accordance with the order of the Appellate Tribunal.

question: What happens if the amount of tax is reduced as a result of the judgment in the reference by the High Court, and the amount of tax found refundable?
answer: The High Court may, on application by the Commissioner within thirty days of the receipt of the judgment of the High Court, make an order authorizing the Commissioner to postpone the refund until the disposal of the appeal by the Supreme Court.

question: What is the fee for an application under this section by a person other than the Commissioner?
answer: One hundred rupees.

question: What is the period within which an order of the High Court staying the recovery of tax ceases to have effect?
answer: Six months following the day on which it was made, unless the appeal is decided or such order is withdrawn by the High Court earlier.

question: What law applies to an application made to the High Court under this section?
answer: Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1908.

question: What is the fee required for an application made to the High Court under sub-section (1) by a person other than the Commissioner?
answer: One hundred rupees.

question: What does sub-section (2) require the statement to the High Court to set out?
answer: The facts, the determination of the Appellate Tribunal, and the question of law which arises out of its order.

question: How long does the Special Bench have to decide a reference under this section?
answer: Within six months from the date of its filing.

question: What is the consequence for the Appellate Tribunal's order if the High Court decides a reference under this section?
answer: The Appellate Tribunal's order shall stand modified accordingly.

question: Who constitutes the Special Bench to hear references under this section?
answer: The Chief Justice constitutes the Special Bench, comprising not less than two judges of the High Court.

question: What is the purpose of establishing a case management system by the High Court?
answer: To ensure that sufficient number of Special Benches are constituted, so as to ensure that a reference filed under this section is decided within the stipulated six months.

question: What is the applicable time frame for the High Court to decide a reference under this section?
answer: Six months from the date of its filing.

question: Can a reference against an order of the Commissioner (Appeals) be made to the High Court?
answer: Yes, if communicated after the date of commencement of the Tax Laws (Amendment) Act, 2024.

question: What is the provision regarding the number of judges in the Special Bench?
answer: The Special Bench shall comprise not less than two judges of the High Court.

question: What is the requirement for the High Court to hear a reference under this section?
answer: The High Court must be satisfied that a question of law arises out of such order referred to in sub-section (1).

question: What is the effect of omitting the expression ‘or, as the case may be, the Commissioner (Appeals)’ in Section 133?
answer: It is omitted by the Finance Act, 2025.

question: What is the amount of fee to be paid with an application under sub-section (1) by the aggrieved person other than the Commissioner?
answer: Fifty thousand rupees.

question: Can the Commissioner file an application under sub-section (1)?
answer: Yes, but it must be accompanied by a written authorization by the relevant Chief Commissioner.

question: What is the procedure for staying tax recovery?
answer: The High Court may stay recovery of tax on an application filed and after affording an opportunity of being heard to the Commissioner, subject to deposit with the assessing authority of not less than thirty percent of the tax determined by the Appellate Tribunal.

question: How long can an order for staying tax recovery remain in effect?
answer: It shall cease to have effect on the expiration of a period of six months following the day on which it was made unless the reference is decided or such order is withdrawn by the High Court earlier.

question: What is the applicable fee for the Commissioner to file an application under sub-section (1)?
answer: No fee is specified for the Commissioner, but a written authorization by the relevant Chief Commissioner is required.

question: How does the Limitation Act, 1908, apply to an application made to the High Court under sub-section (1)?
answer: Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1908, shall apply to an application made to the High Court under sub-section (1).

question: Can the High Court authorize the Commissioner to postpone refund until the disposal of the appeal by the Supreme Court?
answer: Yes, if the amount of tax is reduced as a result of the judgment in the reference and some amount of tax is found to be refundable, the High Court may make an order authorizing the Commissioner to postpone the refund until the disposal of the appeal by the Supreme Court.

question: Can the Commissioner prefer a petition for leave to appeal to the Supreme Court?
answer: Yes, but only if the amount of tax is reduced as a result of the judgment in the reference and some amount of tax is found to be refundable, and the High Court may make an order authorizing the Commissioner to postpone the refund until the disposal of the appeal by the Supreme Court.

question: What is the applicable fee for the Commissioner to file an application under sub-section (1) when an application is made by the aggrieved person other than the Commissioner?
answer: Fifty thousand rupees.

question: What is the requirement for the Commissioner to file an application under section 133?
answer: The Commissioner's application must be accompanied by a written authorization by the relevant Chief Commissioner.

question: Can an appeal be made to the Supreme Court from a High Court decision on a reference made under section 133?
answer: Yes, an appeal can be made to the Supreme Court if the High Court certifies the case as a fit one for appeal.

question: What is the process for an appeal to the Supreme Court under section 134?
answer: The provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, relating to appeals to the Supreme Court apply, and the judgment of the High Court is varied or reversed in appeal, effect is given to the order of the Supreme Court in the manner provided in sub-section (12) of section 133.

question: What is the purpose of section 134A of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001?
answer: Section 134A provides for Alternative Dispute Resolution through the appointment of a committee to resolve disputes related to tax liability, admissibility of refunds, waiver of default surcharge and penalty, and other specific relief required to resolve disputes.

question: Who can apply for the appointment of a committee under section 134A?
answer: An aggrieved person in connection with any dispute pertaining to tax liability, admissibility of refunds, waiver of default surcharge and penalty, or any other specific relief required to resolve the dispute, may apply to the Board for the appointment of a committee.

question: What are the requirements for constituting a committee under section 134A?
answer: The committee must comprise an officer of Inland Revenue not below the rank of a Commissioner, a person nominated by the taxpayer from a panel notified by the Board, a retired Judge not below the rank of District and Sessions Judge, to be nominated through consensus by the members appointed under clauses (i) and (ii).

question: Can a Chartered Accountant or Cost and Management Accountant be nominated by the taxpayer if they have been an auditor or authorized representative of the taxpayer?
answer: No, the taxpayer shall not nominate a Chartered Accountant or Cost and Management Accountant if they are or have been an auditor or authorized representative of the taxpayer.

question: What happens if the order of withdrawal by the court of law or the Appellate Authority is not communicated to the Board within seventy five days of the appointment of the committee?
answer: The committee shall be dissolved and the provisions of this section shall not apply.

question: Can an appeal be pending before any court of law or an Appellate Authority if the committee is appointed under section 134A?
answer: Yes, the aggrieved person, or the Commissioner, or both, as the case may be, shall withdraw the appeal pending before any court of law or an Appellate Authority after the constitution of the committee by the Board under sub-section (2).

question: What kind of relief can be sought through the committee appointed under section 134A?
answer: The committee can provide relief related to tax liability, admissibility of refunds, waiver of default surcharge and penalty, and other specific relief required to resolve the dispute.

question: Who can nominate a retired Judge to be a member of the committee?
answer: The members appointed under clauses (i) and (ii) can nominate a retired Judge not below the rank of District and Sessions Judge through consensus.

question: What happens if the order of withdrawal by the court of law or the Appellate Authority is not communicated within 75 days?
answer: The committee will be dissolved, and the provisions of this section will not apply.

question: How long does the committee have to decide a dispute after its appointment?
answer: The committee shall decide the dispute by majority, within one hundred and twenty days of its appointment.

question: Can the recovery of tax payable by a taxpayer be stayed during the dispute resolution process?
answer: Yes, the recovery of tax payable by a taxpayer in connection with any dispute for which a Committee has been appointed shall be deemed to have been stayed on withdrawal of appeal up to the date of decision by the Committee.

question: What happens if the committee fails to decide within the period of 120 days?
answer: The Board shall dissolve the committee by an order in writing, and the matter shall be decided by the court of law or the Appellate Authority which issued the order of withdrawal.

question: How long does the court of law or the Appellate Authority have to decide the appeal after the order of dissolution is communicated?
answer: The appeal shall be decided within six months of the communication of the said order.

question: Can the aggrieved person make the payment of income tax and other taxes as decided by the committee?
answer: Yes, the aggrieved person may make the payment of income tax and other taxes as decided by the committee under sub-section (5) and all decisions, orders and judgments made or passed shall stand modified to that extent.

question: What is the purpose of the application for dispute resolution under Section 134A?
answer: The purpose of the application is to resolve any hardship or dispute mentioned in detail in the application, which is under litigation in any court of law or an Appellate Authority, except where criminal proceedings have been initiated.

question: What should accompany the application for dispute resolution under Section 134A?
answer: The application should be accompanied by an initial proposition for resolution of the dispute, including an offer of tax payment, from which, the applicant would not be entitled to retract.

question: How long does the Board have to appoint a committee after examining the application under Section 134A?
answer: The Board may appoint a committee within forty-five days after examination of the application of an aggrieved person.

question: What is the condition for a taxpayer to apply for dispute resolution under Section 133?
answer: The applicant is under litigation in a court of law or an Appellate Authority, excluding cases where criminal proceedings have been initiated.

question: What is the deadline for the Board to appoint a committee after receiving an application?
answer: Forty five days

question: Who is eligible to nominate a person from the panel to be part of the committee?
answer: The taxpayer

question: What is the minimum experience required for chartered accountants, cost and management accountants, and advocates on the panel?
answer: Ten years

question: What happens if the member under clause (d) cannot be appointed through consensus?
answer: The Board may nominate a member proposed by the taxpayer

question: What is the timeframe for a court of law or Appellate Authority to withdraw an appeal after the committee is constituted?
answer: After the constitution of the committee

question: What is the consequence if the court of law or Appellate Authority does not communicate the order of withdrawal within seventy five days of the committee's appointment?
answer: The committee is dissolved

question: What is the purpose of the initial proposition for resolution of the dispute that must accompany the application?
answer: Including an offer of tax payment, from which the applicant would not be entitled to retract

question: Can a taxpayer nominate a Chartered Accountant or an advocate if they have been an auditor or an authorized representative of the taxpayer?
answer: No

question: Who are the possible members of the committee according to clause (ii) of the panel?
answer: Chartered accountants, cost and management accountants, and advocates with a minimum of ten years' experience in taxation; officers of the Inland Revenue Service who have retired in BS 21 or above; or reputable businessmen nominated by Chambers of Commerce and Industry

question: What is the purpose of the Committee appointed under sub-section (3)?
answer: The Committee examines the issue and may conduct inquiry, seek expert opinion, direct an audit, and decide the dispute by majority within 120 days of its appointment.

question: What happens if the Committee fails to decide within the period of 120 days?
answer: The Board dissolves the committee, and the matter is decided by the court of law or the Appellate Authority which issued the order of withdrawal, and the appeal is treated as pending as if it had never been withdrawn.

question: What is the recovery period of tax payable by a taxpayer in connection with any dispute for which a Committee has been appointed?
answer: The recovery of tax is deemed to have been stayed on withdrawal of appeal up to the date of decision by the Committee or the dissolution of the Committee, whichever is earlier.

question: What happens if the Committee's decision is not cited or taken as a precedent in any other case or in the same case for a different tax year?
answer: It shall not be cited or taken as a precedent in any other case or in the same case for a different tax year.

question: What is the meaning of State-owned enterprise (SOE) in the context of this section?
answer: State-owned enterprise shall have the same meaning as assigned thereto in the State-Owned Enterprises (Governance)

question: What is the limit of tax liability for a state-owned enterprise (SOE) to apply for the appointment of a committee?
answer: No specific limit is mentioned; an SOE is mandatory to apply for the appointment of a committee for the resolution of any dispute under this section.

question: Can a suit, prosecution, or other legal proceedings be initiated against the SOE or the committee in relation to the dispute resolved under this section?
answer: No, no suit, prosecution, or other legal proceedings shall lie against the SOE or the committee in relation to the dispute resolved under this section.

question: What is the remuneration amount prescribed for the services of the members of the Committee, other than the member appointed under clause (i) of sub-section (3)?
answer: The Board may prescribe the amount.

question: What is the timeframe for the Appellate Authority to decide the appeal after the order of dissolution is communicated to it?
answer: The Appellate Authority shall decide the appeal within six months of the communication of the said order.

question: Can a taxpayer with a tax liability of less than 50 million rupees apply for the appointment of a committee?
answer: No, an aggrieved person in connection with any dispute pertaining to the liability of tax of fifty million rupees or above against the aggrieved person or admissibility of refund may apply for the appointment of a committee.

question: What is the meaning of state-owned enterprise in this context?
answer: A state-owned enterprise shall have the same meaning as assigned thereto in the State-Owned Enterprises (Governance and Operations) Act, 2023 (VII of 2023).

question: Can an aggrieved person apply to the Board for dispute resolution if criminal proceedings have been initiated?
answer: No, an aggrieved person may not apply to the Board for dispute resolution if criminal proceedings have been initiated.

question: What is the mandatory undertaking required from an SOE when applying for dispute resolution?
answer: An SOE must accept the decision of the Committee, which shall be binding on it in all respects, and immediately withdraw any and all pending litigation or cases of any kind in respect of the dispute.

question: How long does the Board have to examine an application for dispute resolution and appoint a committee?
answer: The Board must appoint a committee within fifteen days of receipt of the application.

question: What is the composition of the Committee appointed under sub-section (3)?
answer: The Committee shall comprise a retired judge, the Chief Commissioner Inland Revenue, and a person nominated by the taxpayer from a panel notified by the Board.

question: Can an SOE nominate a chartered accountant or an advocate to the Committee?
answer: No, an SOE may not nominate a chartered accountant or an advocate if the said chartered accountant or the advocate is or has been an auditor or an authorized representative of the SOE.

question: What is the time limit for the Committee to decide the dispute under sub-section (5)?
answer: The Committee shall decide the dispute within forty-five days of its appointment, extendable by another fifteen days for the reasons to be recorded in writing.

question: For how long is the recovery of tax payable by a taxpayer stayed when a Committee is appointed under sub-section (3)?
answer: The recovery of tax payable shall be deemed to have been stayed till the final decision or dissolution of the Committee, whichever is earlier.

question: Can the decision of the Committee under sub-section (5) be cited or taken as a precedent in any other case?
answer: No, the decision of the Committee under sub-section (5) shall not be cited or taken as a precedent in any other case or in the same case for a different tax year.

question: What documents must accompany an application for dispute resolution under sub-section (1)?
answer: The application must be accompanied by an initial proposition for resolution of the dispute, including an offer of tax payment, and an undertaking that the applicant shall accept the decision of the Committee.

question: What is the maximum period for an alternative dispute resolution committee to decide a dispute?
answer: The committee must decide the dispute within sixty days, extendable by another fifteen days for recorded reasons in writing.

question: Is the decision of the alternative dispute resolution committee binding on the Commissioner?
answer: Yes, but only if the aggrieved person withdraws the appeal pending before the court of law or appellate authority within sixty days of the decision being served, and communicates the order of withdrawal to the Commissioner.

question: What happens if the alternative dispute resolution committee fails to decide a dispute within the specified period?
answer: The Board shall dissolve the committee by an order in writing, and the matter shall be decided by the court of law or appellate authority where the dispute is pending under litigation.

question: Can a state-owned enterprise apply for the appointment of an alternative dispute resolution committee?
answer: Yes, and it is mandatory for such enterprises to apply, regardless of the tax liability amount.

question: What is a 'state-owned enterprise'?
answer: A state-owned enterprise has the same meaning as assigned thereto in the State-Owned Enterprises (Governance and Operations) Act, 2023 (VII of 2023).

question: What documents are required to be submitted with an application for alternative dispute resolution?
answer: The application must be accompanied by an initial proposition for resolution of the dispute and an undertaking that the decision of the committee will be binding.

question: What is the deadline for an aggrieved person to withdraw pending cases in respect of a dispute after receiving the decision of the alternative dispute resolution committee?
answer: The decision must be withdrawn within fifteen days of receipt.

question: Can a taxpayer with a tax liability of fifty million rupees or above apply for alternative dispute resolution?
answer: No, but state-owned enterprises are exempt from this limit and are required to apply for resolution.

question: What are the grounds for which a taxpayer may apply for the appointment of an alternative dispute resolution committee?
answer: A taxpayer may apply for resolution of a dispute regarding the liability of tax of fifty million rupees or above or admissibility of refund, or waiver of default surcharge and penalty, or other specific relief required to resolve the dispute.

question: Can criminal proceedings be initiated while an alternative dispute resolution committee is hearing a case?
answer: Yes, but in such cases, the committee may not be appointed under this section.

question: What happens if the Committee fails to decide the dispute within sixty days in the case of a state-owned enterprise?
answer: The Board shall reappoint a Committee under sub-section (3), which shall decide the dispute in accordance with sub-section (5) of this section.

question: Who can be nominated by the taxpayer to be a member of the Committee?
answer: An accountant within the meaning of the Chartered Accountants Ordinance, 1961 (X of 1961); or a cost and management accountant within the meaning of the Cost and Management Accountant Act, 1966 (Act No. XIV of 1966); or an advocate having a minimum of fifteen years' experience in the field of taxation or commercial matters; or an officer of the Inland Revenue who retired in BS 21 or above; or a businessman from a list notified by the Board as recommended by the Federation of Pakistan Chamber of Commerce and Industry.

question: What is the time limit for the court of law or the Appellate Tribunal to decide the appeal after receiving the order of dissolution?
answer: Within ninety days of the communication of the said order.

question: How often should the taxpayer withdraw any and all pending cases of any kind in respect of the dispute?
answer: Within fifteen days of receiving the decision of the Committee.

question: What happens if the Chairman of the Board disagrees with the names proposed by the taxpayer for the Chairperson of the Committee?
answer: The Chairman of the Board shall require the nominees appointed under clause (b) and (c) to propose one name each of a retired judge of a High Court, the Federal Constitutional Court, or the Supreme Court having adequate experience in dealing with tax or commercial matters, and the Chairman shall forward such names to the Federal Minister for Law and Justice for nomination of one of such person as Chairperson of the Committee.

question: Can a chartered accountant or an advocate be nominated by the taxpayer if they are or have been an auditor or an authorized representative of the taxpayer?
answer: No.

question: What is the role of the Board in prescribing the amount to be paid as remuneration for the services of the members of the Committee?
answer: The Board may prescribe the amount to be paid as remuneration for the services of the members of the Committee, other than the member appointed under clause (ii) of sub-section (3).

question: What is the consequence of the decision of the Committee being final and binding on the Commissioner and the state-owned enterprise (SOE) that is directly or indirectly wholly owned by the Federal Government?
answer: The decision of the Committee shall be final and binding on the Commissioner and the SOE.

question: How long does the Chairman of the Board have to appoint a committee after examination of the application of an aggrieved person?
answer: Within fifteen days of receipt of such application by the Board.

question: Who shall be the Chairperson of the Committee?
answer: A retired judge of a High Court, the Federal Constitutional Court, or the Supreme Court having adequate experience in dealing with tax or commercial matters.

question: Who can be a member of the Committee appointed under Section 134A?
answer: The Committee may consist of chartered accountants, advocates with a minimum of fifteen years' experience in taxation or commercial matters, officers of the Inland Revenue who retired in BS 21 or above, and businessmen from a list notified by the Board as recommended by the Federation of Pakistan Chamber of Commerce and Industry.

question: What is the role of the Chairman of the Board regarding the appointment of the Committee?
answer: The Chairman of the Board shall communicate the order of appointment of the Committee to the aggrieved person, court of law or Appellate Tribunal or tax authority where the dispute is pending and to the Commissioner concerned.

question: What is the time limit for the Committee to decide a dispute?
answer: The Committee shall decide the dispute by majority, within ninety days of its appointment.

question: Can the decision of the Committee be cited as a precedent in another case?
answer: No, the decision by the Committee shall not be cited or taken as a precedent in any other case or in the same case for a different tax year.

question: What happens to the recovery of tax payable by a taxpayer when a Committee is appointed?
answer: The recovery of tax payable by a taxpayer in connection with any dispute for which a Committee has been appointed shall be deemed to have been stayed on the constitution of the Committee till the final decision or dissolution of the Committee, whichever is earlier.

question: When will the decision of the Committee be binding on the Commissioner?
answer: The decision of the Committee under sub-section (5) shall be binding on the Commissioner when the aggrieved person, being satisfied with the decision, has withdrawn the appeal pending before the court of law or Appellate Tribunal or tax authority in respect of the dispute, and has communicated the order of withdrawal to the Commissioner.

question: What happens if the order of withdrawal is not communicated to the Commissioner within sixty days?
answer: If the order of withdrawal is not communicated to the Commissioner within sixty days of the service of decision of the Committee upon the aggrieved person, the decision of the Committee shall not be binding on the Commissioner.

question: What is the responsibility of the Commissioner regarding the appeal pending before any court of law or Appellate Tribunal or tax authority?
answer: The Commissioner shall also withdraw the appeal, if any, pending before any court of law or Appellate Tribunal or tax authority in respect of the dispute as mentioned in sub-section (1) within thirty days of the communication of the order of withdrawal by the aggrieved person to the Commissioner.

question: What happens if the Committee fails to decide within the period of ninety days?
answer: If the Committee fails to decide within the period of ninety days, the Chairman of the Board shall dissolve the Committee by an order in writing and the matter shall be decided by the court of law or Appellate Tribunal or tax authority, as the case may be.

question: Can a Special Offense Estate (SOE) directly or indirectly wholly owned by the Federal Government appeal to the Federal Constitutional Court or Supreme Court?
answer: Yes, except an SOE directly or indirectly wholly owned by the Federal Government, either party may prefer an appeal to the Federal Constitutional Court or the Supreme Court, as the case may be, within a period of sixty days against a decision of the Committee or where no decision is made, upon receiving order of dissolution of the Committee.

question: What is the time frame for the Federal Constitutional Court or the Supreme Court to decide on a petition against a decision of the Committee?
answer: A period of sixty days.

question: Can a High Court abate a petition filed by a wholly-owned SOE against the decision of the Committee?
answer: Yes, upon commencement of the Income Tax (Amendment) Act, 2026.

question: How long does a court of law or Appellate Tribunal or tax authority have to decide a case after receiving the order of dissolution of the Committee?
answer: Within ninety days of the communication of the said order.

question: How is the remuneration for the Chairperson of the Committee paid?
answer: The Board and the taxpayer pay the remuneration equally within a period of fifteen days from the constitution of the Committee.

question: Under what circumstances can a Federal Constitutional Court, the Supreme Court, or a High Court refer a dispute to the Board for resolution by the Committee?
answer: On its own motion or on the application of either party, or where both parties agree to refer the dispute for resolution.

question: What happens to disputes of SOEs pending before any court of law or Appellate Tribunal or tax authority upon commencement of the Income Tax (Amendment) Act, 2026?
answer: They stand transferred to the Board for resolution by the Committee to be appointed under sub-section (3).

question: How long does the Board have to appoint a Committee under sub-section (3) after receiving an order or transfer to refer a dispute for resolution?
answer: Within fifteen days from the date of such order or transfer.

question: What is the General Clauses Act, 1897 (X of 1897) subject to in relation to the Income Tax (Amendment) Act, 2026?
answer: The provisions of the Income Tax (Amendment) Act, 2026, subject to section 6.

question: Can a SOE make a fresh application for reconstitution of the Committee in accordance with the provisions of the Income Tax (Amendment) Act, 2026?
answer: Yes, the applicant, including a SOE, may make a fresh application.

question: Who is responsible for paying the remuneration of a nominee under clause (c) of sub-section (3)?
answer: The taxpayer.

question: What is the purpose of appointing a Committee under sub-section (3)?
answer: The purpose of appointing a Committee under sub-section (3) is for resolution of disputes referred or transferred for resolution by the Board.

question: How long does the Board have to appoint the Committee after receiving an order or transfer?
answer: The Board shall appoint the Committee within fifteen days from the date of such order or transfer.

question: What is the relation between the provisions of the Income Tax (Amendment) Act, 2026 and the General Clauses Act, 1897?
answer: The provisions of the Income Tax (Amendment) Act, 2026 are subject to the provisions of section 6 of the General Clauses Act, 1897.

question: Can a SOE apply for reconstitution of the Committee after the enactment of the Income Tax (Amendment) Act, 2026?
answer: Yes, a SOE may make a fresh application for reconstitution of the Committee in accordance with the provisions of the Income Tax (Amendment) Act, 2026, if the Committee has not rendered its decision prior to its enactment.

question: How can the Board make rules for carrying out the purposes of this section?
answer: The Board may make rules for carrying out the purposes of this section by notification in the official Gazette.

question: Can a Committee's decision be made prior to the enactment of the Income Tax (Amendment) Act, 2026?
answer: Yes, if the Committee has not rendered its decision prior to its enactment, a SOE may make a fresh application for reconstitution of the Committee.

question: What is the purpose of the Income Tax (Amendment) Act, 2026?
answer: The provisions of the Income Tax (Amendment) Act, 2026 are subject to the provisions of section 6 of the General Clauses Act, 1897.

question: Is there a time limit for a Committee to render its decision?
answer: No specific time limit is mentioned in the excerpt, but a Committee's decision can be made prior to its enactment if it hasn't been rendered yet.

question: What clause of the Act deals with the transfer of disputes?
answer: Clause (a) deals with the transfer of disputes.

question: What is the relevant Act No. for the Income Tax (Amendment) Act, 2026?
answer: The relevant Act No. for the Income Tax (Amendment) Act, 2026 is IX of 2026.

question: Who bears the burden of proof in an appeal under Part of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001?
answer: The burden shall be on the taxpayer to prove, on the balance of probabilities.

question: What does the Commissioner (Appeals) do in case of an assessment order that requires revision?
answer: The Commissioner (Appeals) may make such revision to the order as the Commissioner thinks fit.

question: Can an order under Section 135 be prejudicial to the person to whom it relates?
answer: No, an order under sub-section (2) shall not be prejudicial to the person to whom the order relates.

question: What fee accompanies an application for the revision of an assessment order under Section 135?
answer: A fee of the lesser of two thousand five hundred rupees or ten per cent of the tax assessed.

question: What are the conditions for the Commissioner to revise an order under Section 135?
answer: The Commissioner shall not revise any order under sub-section (2) if – the time within which an appeal may be made has not expired, or the person has not waived their right of appeal; the order is pending on appeal before the Commissioner (Appeals) or has been made the subject of an appeal to the Appellate Tribunal; or in the case of an application made by a person, the application has not been made within ninety days of the date on which such order was served on the person, unless the Commissioner is satisfied that the person was prevented by sufficient cause from making the application within the time allowed.

question: Can an application for revision of an assessment order be made under Section 135 if the amount of tax due under the assessment is not in dispute?
answer: No, No application for revision of an assessment order may be made under sub-section (1) unless the amount of tax due under the assessment that is not in dispute has been paid by the taxpayer.

question: What is the time limit for making an application under Section 135 if the application is made by a person?
answer: In the case of an application made by a person, the application must be made within ninety days of the date on which such order was served on the person, unless the Commissioner is satisfied that the person was prevented by sufficient cause from making the application within the time allowed.

question: Who pays the fee accompanying an application for the revision of an assessment order under Section 135?
answer: The taxpayer pays the fee accompanying an application for the revision of an assessment order under Section 135.

question: What happens if the Commissioner declines to interfere in an application under Section 135?
answer: An order by the Commissioner declining to interfere shall not be treated as an order prejudicial to the applicant.

question: What is the purpose of Section 135?
answer: Section 135 provides for the Commissioner to call for the record of any proceeding under this Ordinance in which an order has been passed by any taxation officer other than the Commissioner (Appeals), and to make revision to the order as necessary.

question: What is the due date for payment of tax according to the Income Tax Ordinance 2001?
answer: The tax payable by a taxpayer on the taxable income of the taxpayer shall be due on the due date for furnishing the taxpayer’s return of income for that year.

question: How long does a taxpayer have to pay tax after receiving an assessment order?
answer: Fifteen days from the date of the assessment order is issued.

question: What happens if a taxpayer defaults in payment of instalments for tax paid by instalments?
answer: The whole balance of the tax outstanding shall become immediately payable.

question: Can a taxpayer pay tax by instalments?
answer: Yes, the Commissioner may, having regard to the circumstances of the case, allow the taxpayer to pay such tax in instalments of equal or varying amounts.

question: What is the maximum number of days a taxpayer has to pay tax after receiving a notice under sub-section (2)?
answer: Thirty days (previously forty-five days) from the date of service of the notice.

question: Can the Commissioner grant an extension of time for payment of tax due?
answer: Yes, the Commissioner may, where good cause is shown, grant the taxpayer an extension of time for payment of tax due.

question: What happens if a taxpayer pays tax prior to expiry of the period specified in the first proviso to sub-section (2)?
answer: The operation of sub-section (2) shall not be affected.

question: Is the liability for default surcharge arising under section 205 affected by the grant of an extension of time to pay tax due?
answer: No, the grant of an extension of time to pay tax due shall not preclude the liability for default surcharge arising under section 205 from the due date of the tax under sub-section (2).

question: Can a taxpayer apply for an extension of time for payment of tax due?
answer: Yes, a taxpayer may make a written application to the Commissioner for an extension of time for payment of tax due, showing good cause.

question: What is the due date for payment of tax payable under sub-section (7) of section 147?
answer: The date specified in sub-section (5) or sub-section (5A) or the first proviso to sub-section (5B) of section 147.

question: What is the process for recovering tax due from a taxpayer?
answer: The Commissioner serves a notice in the prescribed form requiring the taxpayer to pay the amount within a specified time.

question: What is the maximum period for which a taxpayer can be detained in prison for non-payment of tax?
answer: Six months.

question: What are the modes of recovery available to the Commissioner if the taxpayer fails to pay the amount due?
answer: Attachment and sale of property, appointment of a receiver, arrest and detention in prison for up to six months, and other modes as specified in section 48 of the Sales Tax Act, 1990.

question: What powers does the Commissioner have for the recovery of tax under this section?
answer: The same powers as a Civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, for the recovery of any amount due under a decree.

question: How does the Commissioner proceed to recover tax if the taxpayer has appealed the decision?
answer: The Commissioner proceeds to recover the tax irrespective of the time provided under any other provision or the decision or judgment.

question: What is the limit for tax payable to be recovered under sub-section (3A) of this section?
answer: Rupees two hundred million.

question: What is the process for challenging a decision under sub-section (4) of this section?
answer: The taxpayer may challenge the decision only under Part III of this Chapter.

question: What is the effect of a decision in favor of the department at three appellate forums on the tax payable?
answer: The tax payable becomes immediately payable, subject to certain conditions.

question: What is the role of the Board in regulating the procedure for the recovery of tax under this section?
answer: The Board may make rules regulating the procedure for the recovery of tax and any other matter connected with or incidental to the operation of this section.

question: Can the Commissioner sue for and recover tax due from the taxpayer in any court of competent jurisdiction?
answer: Yes, the Commissioner can sue for and recover tax due from the taxpayer in any court of competent jurisdiction by producing a certificate signed by the Commissioner.

question: What conditions must be met for tax to become immediately payable under Section 138?
answer: The conditions are that the case has been decided in the favor of the department at three appellate forums, including the High Court, and that the recovery must be to the extent of the lowest amount of demand confirmed by any of the three appellate forums.

question: What is the minimum amount of tax payable for recovery through arrest under Section 138?
answer: The tax payable must exceed rupees two hundred million.

question: What happens if the Commissioner determines that the tax payable exceeds rupees two hundred million?
answer: The Commissioner shall proceed to recover the said amount irrespective of the time provided under any other provision or the decision or judgment.

question: Can the Board make rules regulating the recovery of tax under Section 138?
answer: Yes, the Board may make rules regulating the procedure for the recovery of tax under this section and any other matter connected with, or incidental to, the operation of this section.

question: Under what condition will the Commissioner proceed to recover tax without adhering to the usual time constraints?
answer: The Commissioner will proceed to recover tax without adhering to the usual time constraints if the tax payable exceeds rupees two hundred million.

question: How many appellate forums must decide in the favor of the department for tax to become immediately payable?
answer: Three appellate forums, including the High Court.

question: What happens to the recovered amount if the three appellate forums confirm different amounts of demand?
answer: The recovery will be made to the extent of the lowest amount of demand confirmed by any of the three appellate forums.

question: What is the significance of the Finance Act, 2020 in relation to Section 138?
answer: The Finance Act, 2020 made changes to the word "and" and the word "and" thereafter new clause (d) was added, and a full stop was substituted by a semi colon.

question: Can the Board make rules regulating any matter connected with or incidental to the operation of Section 138?
answer: Yes, the Board may make rules regulating any other matter connected with, or incidental to, the operation of this section.

question: What is the effective date of the changes made by the Finance Act, 2020?
answer: The changes made by the Finance Act, 2020 are dated 30th June, 2020.

question: Who forwards a certificate specifying the amount of tax due to the District Officer (Revenue)?
answer: The Commissioner forwards the certificate.

question: What is the purpose of the District Officer (Revenue) receiving a certificate from the Commissioner?
answer: The District Officer (Revenue) proceeds to recover from the taxpayer the amount specified in the certificate.

question: What power does the District Officer (Revenue) have for the recovery of an amount due?
answer: The District Officer (Revenue) has the same powers as a Civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, for the recovery of the amount due under a decree.

question: When does the District Officer (Revenue) have the power to recover an amount due?
answer: The District Officer (Revenue) proceeds to recover from the taxpayer the amount specified in the certificate.

question: What if the taxpayer resides or carries on business in a different district than where the Commissioner resides?
answer: The Commissioner still forwards the certificate to the District Officer (Revenue) of the district in which the taxpayer resides or carries on business or in which any property belonging to the taxpayer is situated.

question: What is the District Officer (Revenue) empowered to recover?
answer: The amount specified in the certificate, as if it were an arrear of land revenue.

question: Can the District Officer (Revenue) use powers other than those mentioned in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908?
answer: Yes, without prejudice to any other power of the District Officer (Revenue), he has the powers mentioned in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

question: What is the legal basis for the District Officer (Revenue)'s power to recover an amount due?
answer: The legal basis is a decree under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

question: What is the scope of the District Officer (Revenue)'s powers for the recovery of an amount due?
answer: The District Officer (Revenue) has the same powers as a Civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

question: Can the District Officer (Revenue) recover an amount due from a taxpayer who does not reside or carry on business in the district?
answer: Yes, if the property belonging to the taxpayer is situated in the district.

question: What happens to a taxpayer's tax liability when they are declared bankrupt?
answer: The tax liability under this Ordinance shall pass on to the estate in bankruptcy.

question: Is estate in bankruptcy considered a taxpayer under this Ordinance?
answer: No, since the tax liability is passed on to the estate in bankruptcy.

question: What happens to tax liability incurred by an estate in bankruptcy?
answer: The tax shall be deemed to be a current expenditure in the operations of the estate in bankruptcy and shall be paid before the claims preferred by other creditors are settled.

question: Is tax liability of an estate in bankruptcy settled first before other creditors?
answer: Yes, after being considered a current expenditure in the operations of the estate in bankruptcy.

question: If I earn a certain income that results in a tax liability, and then I am declared bankrupt, what happens to my tax liability?
answer: The tax liability under this Ordinance shall pass on to the estate in bankruptcy.

question: What happens to the tax liability of an estate in bankruptcy in terms of its claims on other creditors?
answer: The tax liability shall be paid before the claims preferred by other creditors are settled.

question: Is the tax liability of an estate in bankruptcy considered a priority claim?
answer: Yes, as it is to be paid before the claims preferred by other creditors are settled.

question: How should tax liability incurred by an estate in bankruptcy be handled?
answer: As a current expenditure in the operations of the estate in bankruptcy, to be paid before other creditor claims.

question: What is the purpose of deeming tax liability as a current expenditure in the operations of an estate in bankruptcy?
answer: So that it can be paid before the claims preferred by other creditors are settled.

question: Does this Ordinance specify any particular priority of claims for an estate in bankruptcy?
answer: Yes, tax liability is to be paid before the claims preferred by other creditors are settled.

question: Who is jointly and severally liable for payment of tax due by a private company if the tax cannot be recovered from the company?
answer: A director of the company, other than an employed director, and/or a shareholder in the company owning not less than ten per cent of the paid-up capital of the company.

question: Can a director who pays tax under Section 139(1) recover the tax paid from the company?
answer: Yes, the director is entitled to recover the tax paid from the company or a share of the tax from any other director.

question: What is the share of the tax that a shareholder who pays tax under Section 139(1) can recover from other shareholders?
answer: From any other shareholder to whom clause (b) of sub-section (1) applies in proportion to the shares owned by that other shareholder.

question: What happens if any tax payable by a member of an association of persons in respect of the member's share of the income of the association cannot be recovered from the member?
answer: The association shall be liable for the tax due by the member.

question: Is it possible for an association of persons to be jointly and severally liable for payment of tax due by other members?
answer: Yes, every person who was, at any time in that year, a member of the association of persons shall be jointly and severally liable for payment of the tax due by the association of persons.

question: Can a member who pays tax under Section 139(5) recover the tax paid from the association of persons?
answer: Yes, the member is entitled to recover the tax paid from the association of persons or a share of the tax from any other member.

question: Is Section 139(7) valid?
answer: The provisions of this Ordinance shall apply to any amount due under this section as if it were tax due under an assessment order.

question: What happens to the provisions of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001 if any tax payable by a private company or association of persons cannot be recovered?
answer: The provisions of this Ordinance shall apply to any amount due under this section as if it were tax due under an assessment order.

question: Is a shareholder required to pay tax under Section 139(1) if the tax cannot be recovered from another shareholder?
answer: No, only a shareholder owning not less than ten per cent of the paid-up capital of the company is required to pay tax under Section 139(1).

question: Can a director who pays tax under Section 139(1) recover the tax paid from an employed director?
answer: No, only a director other than an employed director can be jointly and severally liable for payment of the tax due by the company.

question: What is considered a taxable event under Section 59B?
